title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 197
paragraphs: These are the Libyan tribes we are able to name; and most of them neither now pay any heed to the king of the Medes, nor did they then. This much more I have to say about this land: it is occupied by four peoples and no more, so far as we know. Of these, two are natives of the soil and the other two not; for the Libyans and the Ethiopians are natives—the first dwelling in the northern parts of Libya, the second in the southern—while the Phoenicians and the Hellenes are newcomers.
